Those issues don't look related to me. My team and I have been experiencing the same issue periodically since a recent update. The Opencode desktop app is unusable since it can't load any of our provider\model\MCP information.  Please fix.

Here is the writeup Claude provided me after I had it scan the logs...

Confirming this on v1.18.10, Windows 11 Enterprise. Intermittent — crashes ~70% of launches, succeeds on warm starts.

Environment
Desktop v1.18.10, Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26100
Custom providers via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible (no built-in API keys)
Issue started after updating from ~v1.18.5 on Monday July 28
Symptoms
Renderer: Failed to finish bootstrap instance TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')
Toast: "Failed to reload [ProjectName] — UnsupportedContentType"
Toast: "Failed to reload [ProjectName] — Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')"
Provider list empty, MCP list empty, model selector shows nothing
Root Cause: Race Condition
The desktop signals server ready when the sidecar HTTP listener opens, but the renderer queries providers before the model catalog is fully populated. Across 41 sessions I can reproduce a perfect correlation between updater-check duration (proxy for cold-start slowness) and the crash:


SESSION          spawn→ready  updater_dur   RESULT
20260731T124118  3.2s         23.1s         CRASH  (renderer crashes 32.8s after ready)
20260731T125545  1.6s         1.8s          clean
20260731T132328  2.2s         2.2s          clean
20260731T132215  1.6s         21.8s         CRASH
20260730T203640  2.4s         1.9s          clean
20260730T202202  2.8s         22.1s         CRASH
Pattern: every session where updater check takes >10s → CRASH. Every session where it completes in <3s → clean. The updater duration isn't the cause — it's a marker for cold-start conditions where the sidecar registry population takes longer than the renderer's bootstrap timeout.

Renderer logs (crash sessions)

[2026-07-31 08:41:55.871] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')
[2026-07-31 08:30:51.103] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')
[2026-07-29 17:15:46.086] [error] Failed to finish bootstrap instance TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'temperature')
Sidecar log (no errors during crash — provider catalog just not ready yet)

timestamp=2026-07-31T12:41:41.058Z level=INFO message=loading path="...opencode.jsonc"
timestamp=2026-07-31T12:41:44.176Z level=INFO message=bootstrapping directory="...WinISO-Builder"
timestamp=2026-07-31T12:41:44.229Z level=INFO message=init
Config loads at :41.058, but init doesn't complete until :44.229 — 3.2s after config load. Renderer crashes at :55.871 — 32.8s after server ready. The renderer queried providers during the initialization window and got an empty/partial map.

What I tried (none fix the issue)
OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH=1 — providers disappear entirely (models.dev catalog is required for custom provider registration)
OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=1 — sidecar fails to start at all
autoupdate: false in opencode.jsonc — no effect on desktop updater (separate electron-updater)
Relaunching repeatedly — eventually hits a warm start and succeeds
Suggested fix
The loading guard added in PR #39445 is incomplete. The TanStack Query isLoading flag reflects HTTP request state, not sidecar catalog readiness. If the sidecar returns successfully but with an empty/partial provider list (because the catalog hasn't finished building), the query resolves "loaded" and the renderer accesses undefined model entries. The guard should check that the provider map is non-empty and contains the persisted model selection before attempting to read model properties like temperature.

For anyone landing here from the bot: this is the ZDR-removal filing. I expanded on the same problem in #39875. The short version of the findings is below.

The two commits:

1. On 2026-07-16, @fwang shipped 5121352 "go: grok 4.5 and kimi k3" and deleted the per-model provider column from `packages/console/app/src/routes/go/index.tsx`. The page used to show e.g. `GLM-5.2 -> DeepInfra, Fireworks AI, Z.ai`. It's a plain `string[]` now. The public API `/zen/go/v1/models` stopped returning a provider field at the same time. I ran `curl https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models | jq '.data[0]'` and got `{"id":"minimax-m3","object":"model","created":1785502284,"owned_by":"opencode"}`. Nothing tells me which upstream serves the model.

2. On 2026-07-31, @fwang shipped 2df47ee "deepseek v4 flash" and softened `go.faq.a5.body` from "Our providers follow a zero-retention policy and do not use your data for model training" to "Your data will not be used for model training". The replacement is strictly weaker. The `go.faq.a5.beforeExceptions` paragraph right below it still says "Providers follow a zero-retention policy". Same FAQ contradicts itself in 17 locales now.

3. The [2026-03-29 OpenCode tweet](https://x.com/opencode/status/2038302829517893825) "we've signed Zero Data Retention agreements with all providers for Go" is still up (512K views). Reverting it quietly with no changelog is much worse than reverting loudly.

4. The deployed model catalog lives in 30 separate SST secrets (`ZEN_MODELS1..30`). The internal `console-go.*` / `inf-go.*` provider IDs are referenced only by `handler.ts` and defined nowhere in the public repo. The `storeModel` schema field is unread anywhere I can grep. After the `dataDumper.ts` file's last touch on 2026-05-21 (commit `6de584f`), the maintainers' 2026-02-19 statement that "storeModel is only set for free models" is unverifiable from public artifacts.

5. The server-side proxy also forwards per-request metadata to Honeycomb and SST Lake (Firehose, Iceberg S3 Tables via Glue, Athena, fronted by an ECS Fargate service at `packages/stats/server`). The fields per request: IP, /32 prefix for IPv4, /64 for IPv6, cf.continent / cf.country / cf.city / cf.region / cf.latitude / cf.longitude / cf.timezone, workspace, user_id, API key, model, real upstream provider (via the `x-opencode-endpoint-id` pass-through at `handler.ts:256-265`), token counts, cost, latency. Basically all the data about the user. Not in the privacy policy.
 **Why do you need my lat+long, my /32 IP, my precise request metadata, for Zen pay-as-you-go, Zen subscription, Go subscription, free trial users, and anonymous rate-limited calls, and why is none of it in the privacy policy?** Why is there no opt-out?

Three of the relevant Go providers, DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax, were caught by Anthropic in February 2026 running TOS-violating distillation attacks against Claude with 16M+ exchanges, 24,000 fraudulent accounts. The implicit trust assumption behind "custom data retention agreements" with these labs is weak.

The ZDR wording has to be either restored, or we should get a public explanation of why it is gone. The per-model provider column has to be back in the API and the UI. There should also be a published confirmation that no Go or Zen paid provider has prompt-content storage. The Honeycomb and SST Lake destinations have to be named in the privacy policy. A binding retention statement has to be in the privacy policy.

Can confirm this independently — reproduced it in isolation with plain `urllib.request` (no SDK, no third-party libs at all):

```python
import urllib.request, json
req = urllib.request.Request(
    "https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions", method="POST",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk-...", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
    data=json.dumps({"model": "big-pickle", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}).encode(),
)
urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15)
```

Result: `403`, body `error code: 1010` (Cloudflare). Switching only the `User-Agent` header to a normal browser string (everything else identical — same key, same body, same endpoint) makes it return `200` immediately. So it's exactly what's described here: the block triggers purely on `User-Agent` starting with `Python-urllib`, before auth is even checked.

This also affects any client built on Python's default HTTP stack (I hit it via the Hermes Agent CLI, which uses `openai`/`httpx` under the hood) — not just raw `urllib`. Worked around it for now with a tiny local reverse proxy that only rewrites `User-Agent`, but it'd be great to get a fix upstream since this silently breaks any Python-based integration against the Zen/Go API.

@awesomekyle Good catch — this matches what we see.

Short answer: **it looks more like a missing/nonstandard stream termination than a clean mid-generation cut.**

We just rechecked both Go endpoints with the same minimal prompt:

`Reply with exactly: LUNA_SSE_TEST`

### 1) Documented path: `POST /zen/go/v1/responses` (stream=true)

This path looks healthier:

- proper Responses SSE event sequence
- text deltas assemble correctly to `LUNA_SSE_TEST`
- ends with `response.output_text.done` → `response.output_item.done` → `response.completed`
- includes usage
- `status: "completed"`

No classic chat-completions `finish_reason` / `[DONE]` here (expected for Responses API).

### 2) Compatibility path: `POST /zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (stream=true)

This is the broken-looking one, and it matches your raw trace closely:

- content deltas arrive (`L` `UNA` `_S` `SE` `_TEST`)
- many chunks have empty `choices: []`
- final usage chunk arrives
- final cost chunk arrives
- **no `data: [DONE]`**
- **no terminal chunk with `finish_reason: "stop"`**
- the only `finish_reason` values seen on content deltas are `null`

Last events look like:

```text
data: {"id":"...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","model":"gpt-5.6-luna","choices":[],"usage":{...}}

data: {"choices":[],"cost":"0"}
```

So: stream has tokens + usage, but clients that require either `[DONE]` or a non-null `finish_reason` will treat it as incomplete and retry (`Stream ended without finish_reason`).

### How this maps to our original report

Our agent client hits the incomplete-stream recovery path (“previous response was cut off… continue”), which then produces:

- exact-phrase repetitions
- junk tails after an already-complete answer
- “already complete” style noise

So the user-visible degradation is likely a **client retry/continue reaction to malformed chat-completions SSE termination on Go Luna**, not only model quality.

### Ask for maintainers

Is Go’s `/chat/completions` stream for `gpt-5.6-luna` intentionally nonstandard, or should it emit a normal OpenAI-compatible terminator (`finish_reason: "stop"` and/or `data: [DONE]`)?

If `/responses` is the supported path for Luna, it would help to call that out more strongly for third-party clients — docs already list Responses for Luna, but many agents still default to chat-completions.

Happy to provide additional redacted SSE captures if useful.

## Executive Summary

The 9.5-hour endurance test demonstrates that the core `runLoop` architecture is stable, deterministic, and functionally sound under prolonged load, successfully completing 195+ steps with zero basic system failures. Post-test manual interruption exposed an edge case: a compounding infinite loop triggered by context size overflow (149,690 > 131,072 tokens). This creates a cycle where message history grows by 2 messages per iteration, increasing the overall context size.

Second demo, this one exercising the new `storage.memory` API (real headless run of this branch via opencode-drive; file writes, hot reloads, and physics are real):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a246264-9d91-4376-a7fa-7e6e9e35b609

1. The agent creates a bouncing-ball toy in the `session.composer.top` slot. Ball state (positions, velocities) lives in `context.storage.memory`, physics runs on an interval that mutates the store.
2. A restyle hot-swaps the plugin — double borders, cycling colors — and the ball keeps its position and velocity through the reload, because old and new generations share the same live memory store.
3. A third edit grows it to five balls with elastic collisions; the original ball never resets.

Building this surfaced a real rendering bug that predates this PR: plugin slot renders were invoked inside a tracked host scope, so any reactive read re-executed the whole render body (resetting plugin-local signals and churning intervals). Fixed in 80532b9c76 by invoking plugin renders through `createComponent` with reactive props. A deeper follow-up remains (child expressions still resolve in a host-tracked scope, so store-driven updates currently remount the slot component per frame rather than updating fine-grained) — tracked separately with full instrumentation notes.

I opened a narrower PR that may help with part of this use case: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/39905

It does not persist system prompts into session exports and does not change transcript storage. Instead, it adds a lightweight local CLI debug command:

```bash
opencode debug prompt
```

The command prints the resolved effective system prompt for the current project/agent/model, including the model base prompt, environment block, instruction files, MCP instructions, available skills, and `experimental.chat.system.transform` plugin modifications.

This is intended as a smaller debugging primitive for verifying what prompt layers are active, without adding DB persistence or a full context/request dump.

Another workaround is to put a local gateway between OpenCode and the vLLM
endpoint. The gateway can accumulate the tool call across chunks instead of
passing each `function.name: null` through to OpenCode.

In [Swobu](https://swobu.com/), create a workspace such as `opencode` with one
route:

| Route | Backend model | Backend URL | Protocol |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local-tools` | your vLLM model | your vLLM `/v1` URL | Streaming Chat Completions |

Then point OpenCode's OpenAI-compatible provider at the workspace:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "model": "swobu/local-tools",
  "provider": {
    "swobu": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Swobu",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:7926/c/opencode/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "local-tools": {
          "name": "Local tools"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

I replayed the stream from this issue through that path. Swobu retained
`read_file` from the first chunk, combined the later argument chunks into
`{"path":"test.py"}`, and returned a tool-call stream with no
`function.name: null` values.

The target protocol must be **Streaming Chat Completions**. This works around
the chunk-validation problem; it does not fix OpenCode or change the vLLM
parser. The model and backend still need to produce an otherwise valid tool
call.

Disclosure: I maintain Swobu. If you try this, I would welcome hearing whether
it works with your OpenCode/vLLM setup. For a Swobu-specific failure, please
share the error and stream shape at
[github.com/swobuforge/swobu](https://github.com/swobuforge/swobu), and I will
help investigate.

Round 3 fixes in fb9e9b2b44, addressing six findings from an out-of-band review:

1. **Setup failures no longer discard the last good generation.** The swap loop snapshots the running registration before overwriting it; if the replacement's `setup()` throws, the previous version is restored and reactivated, with the same `(previous version still active)` state message import failures use. New regression test ("a save whose setup throws restores the previous version"), verified to fail against the old code.
2. **All lifecycle mutations share one serialization chain.** Manual `activate`/`deactivate` from the plugins dialog now enqueue onto the same `loading` chain as watch/config reconciles, so a dialog toggle mid-reload can no longer interleave with a generation swap. Shutdown already awaited the chain, so it now covers manual ops too.
3. **Cleanup failures surface instead of vanishing.** The swallowed `deactivate().catch(() => undefined)` sites now toast (`<id>: cleanup failed: ...`). The swap still proceeds, one broken cleanup should not block a reload, but it is no longer silent. The PR body's earlier claim that these were "logged into states" was wrong; corrected here.
4. **Symlinked plugins reload on target edits.** The watcher lstats each source and, for symlinks, also watches the resolved target path. Discovery already accepted symlinks; now editing the target actually triggers a reload. New e2e test, also verified to fail against the old watcher.
5. **Replaced watched directories re-arm.** On an event for a directory that no longer exists (Linux emits `rename`, not `error`, for this), the watcher closes, forgets the path, and schedules a reconcile so the recreated directory gets a fresh watch.
6. **The crash test asserts its preconditions.** Both readiness polls are now hard assertions, so the test fails if the crashing plugin never loads. Render containment itself (boundary fallback + toast) is documented as not exercisable under the test renderer, which never executes slot render bodies; it is verified in the real TUI and the demo runs above.

Additional data point: the missing termination is not limited to SSE streaming — it reproduces in plain non-stream requests too.

Tested both endpoints with the same minimal prompt (`Reply with exactly: LUNA_OK`), non-stream:

**1) POST /zen/go/v1/responses**
- HTTP 200
- `status: "completed"`
- output text exactly `LUNA_OK`
- clean completion, usage present

**2) POST /zen/go/v1/chat/completions**
- HTTP 200
- `content: "LUNA_OK"`
- **`finish_reason: null`** (no `stop` even on a fully completed response)

So on the compatibility path the model produces the full answer but never emits a terminal `finish_reason`, which forces clients to treat every response as incomplete and retry. This aligns with the streaming trace above (no `[DONE]`, final usage chunk only) and confirms the issue is in the chat/completions transport itself, not in stream handling.

We hit this exact symptom (blank TUI, clean reinstall did not help, macOS). Root cause was NOT the install: it was an external plugin plus a broken config, both of which survive reinstallation.

- `opencode --pure` rendered fine -> external plugin loading was the culprit (`--pure` skips external plugins, so it doubles as a diagnostic).
- `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` had entries in the `plugin` array (a git-installed plugin) and the file contained a trailing comma -> invalid JSON makes plugin init fail silently, and the TUI comes up blank with no error.
- The plugin cache at `~/.cache/opencode/packages/` still held the stale plugin repo, so even config edits alone were not enough until that was removed.

Fix that worked:
1. Run `opencode --pure` to confirm it is plugin/config related.
2. Remove the `plugin` entries from `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and validate the JSON (a single syntax error silences plugin loading).
3. `rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/packages/` to clear the cached plugin.
4. No reinstall needed; sessions in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` are untouched.

Worth adding to the troubleshooting docs: "blank TUI -> try `opencode --pure` first, then inspect the `plugin` array and JSON validity in the config."

Same class of failure here, confirming the root cause wolfie82 identified. Our blank-TUI case (opencode 1.18.10, macOS, Apple Terminal) was caused by a plugin loaded via the `plugin` array in `opencode.json` (installed from a git URL) combined with invalid JSON in the config (a trailing comma). Result: silent plugin init failure -> blank screen with no error.

Diagnostics + fix that worked for us:

1. `opencode --pure` renders fine -> confirms it is plugin/config-related (`--pure` skips external plugins, which makes it a great diagnostic).
2. Remove the offending entries from the `plugin` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and validate the file (`python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('...'))"`). A syntax error in the config silently aborts plugin loading.
3. Delete the plugin cache: `rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/packages/` (stale cached plugin repos survive and get re-loaded).
4. No uninstall/reinstall needed; the session database (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) was never touched.

Suggesting the maintainers keep `--pure`-style plugin skipping as a documented troubleshooting step in the blank-screen issues, since the failure mode is invisible otherwise.
